explain.say: Push the corner of a square frame made of four sticks with loose pins and it folds flat. Do the same to a triangle and it will not budge. That is why engineers build frames out of triangles.

Once the three side lengths of a triangle are fixed, its angles are fixed too. The only way to squash it is to stretch or crush one of the sides, and a strong bar resists that.

faq.q: Why can't a triangle change shape?
faq.a: Three sides of fixed length can only fit together one way, so the angles are locked. To change the shape you would have to stretch or shorten a side.

faq.q: Why does a square frame wobble?
faq.a: A square of four bars joined by pins can lean over into a diamond without any bar changing length. The joints just turn, so it gives way with a small push.
asks: Why is a square weaker than a triangle?

faq.q: What does it mean that a truss bar is only pushed or pulled?
faq.a: In a triangle the load travels along the bars, so each bar is either squeezed, called compression, or stretched, called tension. A bar carries far more load along its length than when bent sideways.
asks: Tension and compression in a triangle

faq.q: What does a diagonal brace do?
faq.a: A diagonal brace cuts a rectangle into two triangles. Now the frame can't lean over without stretching or squashing the brace, so it stays square.
asks: Why do gates have a diagonal bar?

faq.q: Where can I see triangles in structures?
faq.a: Look at truss bridges, crane arms, electricity pylons, roof trusses, the Eiffel Tower and bicycle frames. Each uses triangles to stay stiff while using little material.

facts: A triangle is the only polygon that stays rigid when its corners are free-turning pin joints.
The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice of over 18,000 pieces held together by about 2.5 million rivets.

quiz.say: A rectangular farm gate keeps sagging out of shape. What is the best fix?
quiz.show: A rectangular gate sags. Best fix?
quiz.why: A diagonal bar splits the rectangle into two triangles, which cannot change shape without a bar changing length.

wrong.1: Thicker bars still meet at corners that can turn, so the frame can still lean.
wrong.2: More hinges let the frame move even more easily.
